Record Class ChaosSelector.MethodSelector

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api.ChaosSelector.MethodSelector
Record Components:
operations - operation types this selector matches
classPattern - pattern matched against the declaring class name
methodNamePattern - pattern matched against the method name
signaturePattern - pattern matched against the JVM method descriptor; null for any
All Implemented Interfaces:
ChaosSelector
Enclosing interface:
ChaosSelector
public static record ChaosSelector.MethodSelector(Set<OperationType> operations, NamePattern classPattern, NamePattern methodNamePattern, NamePattern signaturePattern) extends Record implements ChaosSelector
Matches entry to or exit from any method matching the class and method name patterns.

This is the most powerful selector in the API. Combined with ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect and OperationType.METHOD_ENTER it can inject faults into any method in any library without prior preparation. Combined with ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect and OperationType.METHOD_EXIT it corrupts return values on exit.

Automatic weaving. With the agent attached, activating a scenario with this selector weaves entry and exit hooks into every concrete method the patterns name, in classes already loaded and in classes loaded later; removing the scenario (closing its handle, or replacing it) removes them. Constructors, static initialisers, abstract, native, synthetic and bridge methods are never woven, nor are the agent's own classes. Without the agent (a plain ChaosRuntime in a unit test) the events must come from the application's own interception through ChaosRuntime.beforeMethodEnter / afterMethodExit.

Safety constraint: at least one of classPattern or methodNamePattern must be non-ANY. A fully wildcard selector would instrument every method in the JVM. Prefer NamePattern.exact(String) or NamePattern.prefix(String) class patterns: every class loaded while the scenario is active is tested against the class pattern.

signaturePattern is matched against the method's JVM descriptor, e.g. (Ljava/lang/String;I)V for void m(String, int), so it can pick one overload: NamePattern.prefix("(Ljava/lang/String;)"). Events raised through the manual hooks carry no descriptor and never match a non-ANY signature pattern.

Valid operations: OperationType.METHOD_ENTER, OperationType.METHOD_EXIT.
